Faithfully flat quotient morphisms by GaG_{a}-actions on factorial affine varietiesThanks: Supported by JSPS KAKENHI Grant number JP20K03570, JP25K06945.

Kayo Masuda Address: Department of Mathematical Sciences, School of Science, Kwansei Gakuin University
1 Gakuen Uegahara, Sanda 669-1330, Japan Email address: kayo@kwansei.ac.jp
Abstract.

Let XX be a factorial complex affine variety of dimension ≥3\geq 3 with an algebraic action of the additive group GaG_{a}. Let π:X→Y\pi:X\to Y be the algebraic quotient morphism where we assume YY is an affine variety. When π\pi is faithfully flat, we investigate π\pi by GaG_{a}-equivariant affine modifications and give criteria for π\pi to be a trivial 𝔸1{\mathbb{A}}^{1}-bundle. For a smooth acyclic fourfold XX with a free GaG_{a}-action and a GaG_{a}-equivariant 𝔸3{\mathbb{A}}^{3}-fibration f:X→𝔸1f:X\to{\mathbb{A}}^{1} where GaG_{a} acts trivially on 𝔸1{\mathbb{A}}^{1}, we give a criterion for the algebraic quotient YY to be isomorphic to 𝔸3{\mathbb{A}}^{3} with ff as a coordinate. Together with a criterion for π:X→Y\pi:X\to Y to be a trivial 𝔸1{\mathbb{A}}^{1}-bundle, we obtain a sufficient condition for X≅Y×𝔸1≅𝔸4X\cong Y\times{\mathbb{A}}^{1}\cong{\mathbb{A}}^{4}.

Key words and phrases: 
additive group action, 𝔸n{\mathbb{A}}^{n}-fibration, algebraic quotient morphism
2020 Mathematics Subject Classification
Primary: 14R20; Secondary: 14R25, 14L30

1. Introduction

Let X=Spec​BX={\rm Spec}\;B be an affine algebraic variety defined over ℂ{\mathbb{C}} with a non-trivial action of the additive group GaG_{a}. There is a non-trivial locally nilpotent derivation (abbreviated to lnd) δ\delta on BB associated with the GaG_{a}-action on XX. Let A=Ker​δA={\rm Ker}\>\delta. The subalgebra AA of BB is finitely generated over ℂ{\mathbb{C}} if dimX≤3\dim X\leq 3 by the Zariski finiteness theorem [30], however, if dimX>3\dim X>3, AA is not necessarily an affine ℂ{\mathbb{C}}-domain. The morphism π:X→Y=Spec​A\pi:X\to Y={\rm Spec}\;A of affine schemes induced by the inclusion A↪BA\hookrightarrow B is called the algebraic quotient morphism, which we call simply the quotient morphism in this article. The quotient morphism π:X→Y\pi:X\to Y is an 𝔸1{\mathbb{A}}^{1}-fibration whose general closed fiber is a GaG_{a}-orbit. The quotient morphism π\pi is not necessarily equi-dimensional nor surjective even though YY is an affine variety and the GaG_{a}-action on XX is free, i.e., XX has no GaG_{a}-fixed points (for example, see Winkelmann [29]).

An affine nn-space 𝔸n{\mathbb{A}}^{n} for n≤3n\leq 3 can be characterized by a non-trivial GaG_{a}-action. If an affine curve XX admits a GaG_{a}-action, XX is isomorphic to affine line 𝔸1{\mathbb{A}}^{1}. If an affine surface X=Spec​BX={\rm Spec}\;B is factorial, i.e., BB is a UFD, the group B∗B^{*} of invertible elements of BB is ℂ∗{\mathbb{C}}^{*} and XX admits a GaG_{a}-action, then X≅𝔸2X\cong{\mathbb{A}}^{2} by Miyanishi [24]. If an affine threefold X=Spec​BX={\rm Spec}\;B is smooth, acyclic, i.e., Hi​(X,ℤ)=0H_{i}(X,{\mathbb{Z}})=0 for every i>0i>0, and there exists an 𝔸2{\mathbb{A}}^{2}-fibration f:X→𝔸1f:X\to{\mathbb{A}}^{1} such that every closed fiber is factorial, then X≅𝔸3X\cong{\mathbb{A}}^{3} (Miyanishi [23], Kaliman [18], cf. Theorem 4.1). Note that any smooth acyclic affine variety Z=Spec​RZ={\rm Spec}\;R is factorial and R∗=ℂ∗R^{*}={\mathbb{C}}^{*} by Fujita [7, 1.18-1.20] (see also [14, 3.2]). In the case that X=𝔸nX={\mathbb{A}}^{n} for n≤3n\leq 3, Y=𝔸n−1Y={\mathbb{A}}^{n-1} and the quotient morphism π:𝔸n→𝔸n−1\pi:{\mathbb{A}}^{n}\to{\mathbb{A}}^{n-1} is faithfully flat, hence equi-dimensional and surjective (see [3], [5] for n=3n=3). Further, every free GaG_{a}-action on 𝔸n{\mathbb{A}}^{n} for n≤3n\leq 3 is a translation, i.e., π:X→Y\pi:X\to Y is a trivial 𝔸1{\mathbb{A}}^{1}-bundle (for n=3n=3, see [15]). For n=4n=4, a proper GaG_{a}-action on 𝔸4{\mathbb{A}}^{4} preserving a coordinate is a translation by Kaliman [19]. A GaG_{a}-action on XX is proper iff the morphism Ga×X∋(t,x)↦(x,t⋅x)∈X×XG_{a}\times X\ni(t,x)\mapsto(x,t\cdot x)\in X\times X is proper. A proper GaG_{a}-action is free. However, for n≥4n\geq 4, the situation is completely different. In fact, the quotient morphism by a proper GaG_{a}-action is not necessarily equi-dimensional nor surjective as shown by one of Winkelmann’s examples [29]. The example is a GaG_{a}-action on 𝔸5{\mathbb{A}}^{5} preserving two coordinates which is proper but not a translation. Hence if we investigate when the quotient morphism π:𝔸n→Y\pi:{\mathbb{A}}^{n}\to Y is a trivial 𝔸1{\mathbb{A}}^{1}-bundle for n≥4n\geq 4, we should consider under some condition, say, π\pi is faithfully flat or, equi-dimensional and surjective.

In this article, we study the quotient morphism π:X→Y\pi:X\to Y by a GaG_{a}-action on a factorial affine variety XX of dimension ≥3\geq 3. We investigate π\pi under the assumption that YY is an affine variety and π\pi is faithfully flat. When π\pi is faithfully flat, the set Sing⁡(π)={Q∈Y∣π∗​(Q)≇𝔸1}{\rm Sing}(\pi)=\{Q\in Y\mid\pi^{*}(Q)\not\cong{\mathbb{A}}^{1}\} is empty or of pure codimension one in YY ([20], Proposition 2.5 and its remark). If Sing⁡(π)=∅{\rm Sing}(\pi)=\emptyset, π\pi is a trivial 𝔸1{\mathbb{A}}^{1}-bundle (ibid). In the case that XX is smooth and the GaG_{a}-action on XX is free, if π:X→Y\pi:X\to Y is equi-dimensional and surjective, then π\pi is faithfully flat (Proposition 2.5). We give criteria for a faithfully flat π:X→Y\pi:X\to Y to be a trivial 𝔸1{\mathbb{A}}^{1}-bundle in view of the geometry of GaG_{a}-actions (Theorems 3.5, 3.6). We also give a simple proof to the characterization of 𝔸3{\mathbb{A}}^{3} stated above (Theorem 4.1). Let XX be a smooth acyclic fourfold with a free GaG_{a}-action and a GaG_{a}-equivariant 𝔸3{\mathbb{A}}^{3}-fibration f:X→𝔸1f:X\to{\mathbb{A}}^{1} where GaG_{a} acts on 𝔸1{\mathbb{A}}^{1} trivially. Using the characterization of 𝔸3{\mathbb{A}}^{3}, we show that Y≅𝔸3Y\cong{\mathbb{A}}^{3} and ff is a coordinate of Y=𝔸3Y={\mathbb{A}}^{3} under the assumptions that the quotient morphism π:X→Y\pi:X\to Y is equi-dimensional and surjective, YY is an acyclic affine variety and every closed fiber of the morphism fY:Y→𝔸1f_{Y}:Y\to{\mathbb{A}}^{1} induced by ff is factorial (Theorem 4.3). Further, if a criterion for π\pi to be a trivial 𝔸1{\mathbb{A}}^{1}-bundle is satisfied, then X≅Y×𝔸1≅𝔸4X\cong Y\times{\mathbb{A}}^{1}\cong{\mathbb{A}}^{4}.

The construction of this article is as follows. After reviewing quotient morphisms by GaG_{a}-actions in Section 2, we analyze faithfully flat π:X→Y\pi:X\to Y by GaG_{a}-equivariant affine modifications and describe the GaG_{a}-action on XX in Lemmas 3.3 and 3.4. The criteria for π\pi to be a trivial 𝔸1{\mathbb{A}}^{1}-bundle are given in Theorems 3.5 and 3.6. In Section 4, we consider the case that XX is smooth and acyclic. We give a simple proof to the characterization of 𝔸3{\mathbb{A}}^{3} in Theorem 4.1. Finally, we study a smooth acyclic fourfold XX with a free GaG_{a}-action and a GaG_{a}-equivariant 𝔸3{\mathbb{A}}^{3}-fibration f:X→𝔸1f:X\to{\mathbb{A}}^{1}. We give a criterion for Y≅𝔸3Y\cong{\mathbb{A}}^{3} in Theorem 4.3. By a criterion for π:X→Y\pi:X\to Y to be a trivial 𝔸1{\mathbb{A}}^{1}-bundle, we obtain a sufficient condition for X≅Y×𝔸1≅𝔸4X\cong Y\times{\mathbb{A}}^{1}\cong{\mathbb{A}}^{4}.

2. Quotient morphisms by GaG_{a}-actions

We review some facts on GaG_{a}-actions and the quotient morphisms. For general references, we refer to [13] and [6].

Let X=Spec​BX={\rm Spec}\;B be an affine variety with a non-trivial GaG_{a}-action associated with an lnd δ\delta on the affine ℂ{\mathbb{C}}-domain BB. Let A=Ker​δA={\rm Ker}\>\delta and Y=Spec​AY={\rm Spec}\;A. The subalgebra AA of BB is factorially closed in BB, i.e., for b1,b2∈Bb_{1},b_{2}\in B, b1​b2∈A∖{0}b_{1}b_{2}\in A\setminus\{0\} implies b1,b2∈Ab_{1},b_{2}\in A. Hence if XX is factorial (resp. normal), then YY is factorial (resp. normal) as well. Further, A∗=B∗A^{*}=B^{*}. There exists z∈Bz\in B, which is transcendental over AA, such that δ⁡(z)=a∈A∖{0}\delta(z)=a\in A\setminus\{0\} and B⁡[a−1]=A⁡[a−1]​[z]B[a^{-1}]=A[a^{-1}][z]. Such an element z∈Bz\in B is called a local slice of δ\delta. If δ⁡(z)=1\delta(z)=1, zz is called a slice. The ideal δ⁡(B)∩A\delta(B)\cap A of AA is called the plinth ideal and denoted by pl⁡(δ){\rm pl}(\delta). The quotient morphism π:X→Y\pi:X\to Y is defined by the inclusion A↪BA\hookrightarrow B. Note that the closed subset V⁡(pl⁡(δ))V({\rm pl}(\delta)) of YY contains Sing⁡(π){\rm Sing}(\pi).

An lnd δ\delta on BB is called irreducible iff δ⁡(B)⊂b​B\delta(B)\subset bB for b∈Bb\in B implies b∈B∗b\in B^{*}. There exist an irreducible lnd δ~\tilde{\delta} on BB and an element a∈Ker​δ~a\in{\rm Ker}\>\tilde{\delta} such that δ=a​δ~\delta=a\tilde{\delta} [6, Principle 7, Proposition 2.2]. Note that Ker​δ=Ker​δ~{\rm Ker}\>\delta={\rm Ker}\>\tilde{\delta}. Hence the quotient morphism induced by the lnd δ~\tilde{\delta} coincides with the one by δ\delta.

The fixed point locus XGaX^{G_{a}} is defined by the ideal generated by δ⁡(B)\delta(B). Hence if BB is factorial and δ\delta is irreducible, then XGaX^{G_{a}} has codimension >1>1. By a result of Białynicki-Birula [2, Corollary 4], XX has no isolated fixed points.

Lemma 2.1.

Let XX be a factorial affine surface with a GaG_{a}-action associated with an irreducible lnd. Then XX is smooth and has no fixed points.

Proof. Since dimXGa<1\dim X^{G_{a}}<1 as remarked above, it follows from [2] that XGa=∅X^{G_{a}}=\emptyset. The GaG_{a}-action σ:Ga×X→X\sigma:G_{a}\times X\to X induces the automorphism X∋P↦σ⁡(t,P)∈XX\ni P\mapsto\sigma(t,P)\in X for t∈Gat\in G_{a}. If P∈XP\in X is a singular point, then σ⁡(t,P)\sigma(t,P) is a singular point as well. Since XX is normal, the singular locus of XX is of codimension >1>1. Hence if a singular point of XX exists, it must be a fixed point. It follows from XGa=∅X^{G_{a}}=\emptyset that XX is nonsingular. ∎

Let q:X→Yq:X\to Y be an 𝔸1{\mathbb{A}}^{1}-fibration. A fiber q∗​(Q)q^{*}(Q) over a point Q∈YQ\in Y is singular if it is not isomorphic to 𝔸1{\mathbb{A}}^{1}. Let FF be a singular fiber of qq and F=∑i=1rFiF=\sum_{i=1}^{r}F_{i} be the decomposition into irreducible components. An irreducible component FiF_{i} is a multiple fiber component of qq if the multiplicity of FiF_{i} is greater than one.

Theorem 2.2.

([10, Theorem 4.11], [13, Corollary 3.1.39]) Let XX be a smooth affine variety with a non-trivial GaG_{a}-action and let π:X→Y\pi:X\to Y be the quotient morphism where we assume YY is an affine variety. Suppose that π\pi is equi-dimensional. Then the following assertions hold.

  1. (1)

    Every multiple fiber component of π\pi is contained in XGaX^{G_{a}}.

  2. (2)

    Every reduced closed fiber F≠∅F\neq\emptyset of π\pi consists of a disjoint union of 𝔸1{\mathbb{A}}^{1}’s.

Proof. (1) follows from [10, Theorem 4.11].

(2) Since π\pi is equi-dimensional, every closed fiber of π\pi has pure dimension one. Then the assertion follows from [13, Corollary 3.1.39]. ∎

If the GaG_{a}-action on XX is free in Theorem 2.2, then there are no multiple fiber components of π\pi and every closed fiber of π\pi is reduced. Hence every closed fiber consists of a disjoint union of 𝔸1{\mathbb{A}}^{1}’s.

If XX is a normal affine surface, then π\pi is surjective by [11]. If XX is a factorial affine nn-fold for n≤3n\leq 3, then π\pi is equi-dimensional (ibid.). Hence if XX is a smooth acyclic affine threefold, π\pi is equi-dimensional, and also surjective by Kaliman [15, Remark 3.3]. Kaliman and Saveliev [16] showed that if XX is a smooth contractible affine threefold with a free GaG_{a}-action, then π:X→Y\pi:X\to Y is a trivial 𝔸1{\mathbb{A}}^{1}-bundle and X≅Y×𝔸1X\cong Y\times{\mathbb{A}}^{1}. As remarked in Section one, when dimX>3\dim X>3, π\pi is not necessarily equi-dimensional nor surjective even if the action is free.

As for a faithfully flat 𝔸1{\mathbb{A}}^{1}-fibration, the following holds.

Proposition 2.3.

([13, Corollary 2.1.5]) Let q:X→Yq:X\to Y be a faithfully flat fibration of affine varieties. If YY is normal and every closed fiber q∗​(Q)q^{*}(Q) for Q∈YQ\in Y is isomorphic to 𝔸1{\mathbb{A}}^{1}, then qq is an 𝔸1{\mathbb{A}}^{1}-bundle.

As for the smoothness of the base space YY of the quotient morphism π:X→Y\pi:X\to Y, we have the following result. The proof is essentially the same as the one of [9, Lemma 2.22].

Proposition 2.4.

(cf. [9, Lemma 2.22]) Let q:X→Yq:X\to Y be a dominant morphism from an algebraic variety XX of dimension n+rn+r to an algebraic variety YY of dimension nn. Let Q∈YQ\in Y. Suppose that YY is normal at QQ and the fiber q∗​(Q)q^{*}(Q) has an irreducible component FF which is reduced and rr-dimensional. If there exists a point P∈FP\in F at which XX and FF are smooth, then QQ is a smooth point of YY.

By Theorem 2.2 and Proposition 2.4, the following holds.

Proposition 2.5.

Let XX be a smooth affine variety of dimension ≥3\geq 3 with a non-trivial GaG_{a}-action and let π:X→Y\pi:X\to Y be the quotient morphism where we assume YY is an affine variety. Suppose that π\pi is surjective and equi-dimensional. Then the following assertions hold.

  1. (1)

    If the GaG_{a}-action on XX is free, then YY is smooth and π\pi is faithfully flat.

  2. (2)

    If YY is smooth and Sing⁡(π)=∅{\rm Sing}(\pi)=\emptyset, π\pi is an 𝔸1{\mathbb{A}}^{1}-bundle.

  3. (3)

    Suppose that XX is factorial and YY is smooth. Then the plinth ideal pl⁡(δ){\rm pl}(\delta) is principal. If Sing⁡(π)=∅{\rm Sing}(\pi)=\emptyset, then π\pi is a trivial 𝔸1{\mathbb{A}}^{1}-bundle. If Sing⁡(π)≠∅{\rm Sing}(\pi)\neq\emptyset, then the closure Sing⁡(π)¯\overline{{\rm Sing}(\pi)} coincides with V⁡(pl⁡(δ))V({\rm pl}(\delta)) and Sing⁡(π){\rm Sing}(\pi) is of pure codimension one in YY.

Proof. (1) If the GaG_{a}-action is free, then every closed fiber is reduced by Theorem 2.2. Hence YY is smooth by Proposition 2.4. Then π\pi is faithfully flat [21].

(2) Since YY is smooth, π\pi is faithfully flat (ibid.). The assertion follows from Proposition 2.3.

(3) Let δ\delta be the lnd associated with the GaG_{a}-action. Since YY is smooth, π\pi is faithfully flat. Then pl⁡(δ){\rm pl}(\delta) is principal by [20]. If Sing⁡(π)=∅{\rm Sing}(\pi)=\emptyset, then π\pi is a trivial 𝔸1{\mathbb{A}}^{1}-bundle by [20, Corollary 3.4]. Suppose Sing⁡(π)≠∅{\rm Sing}(\pi)\neq\emptyset. We may assume δ\delta is irreducible. Since Sing⁡(π)⊂V⁡(pl⁡(δ)){\rm Sing}(\pi)\subset V({\rm pl}(\delta)) and each irreducible component of V⁡(pl⁡(δ))V({\rm pl}(\delta)) is contained in Sing⁡(π)¯\overline{{\rm Sing}(\pi)} by [20, Theorem 3.3], we have Sing⁡(π)¯=V⁡(pl⁡(δ))\overline{{\rm Sing}(\pi)}=V({\rm pl}(\delta)) and the assertion follows. ∎

Remark. Let X=Spec​BX={\rm Spec}\;B be a factorial affine variety with a GaG_{a}-action associated with an irreducible lnd δ\delta and let A=Ker​δA={\rm Ker}\>\delta. If BB is faithfully flat over AA, then the plinth ideal pl⁡(δ){\rm pl}(\delta) is principal (cf. [20, Lemma 2.1]). Then Sing⁡(π)¯=V⁡(pl⁡(δ))\overline{{\rm Sing}(\pi)}=V({\rm pl}(\delta)) by the same argument as in Proposition 2.5 (3).

By the same argument as in the proof of [12, Theorem 2.1], we have the following result.

Proposition 2.6.

(cf.[12, Theorem 2.1]) Let XX be a smooth acyclic nn-fold for n≥3n\geq 3 and let p:X→𝔸1p:X\to{\mathbb{A}}^{1} be a faithfully flat morphism. Suppose that pp restricts to a trivial 𝔸n−1{\mathbb{A}}^{n-1}-bundle p|p−1​(C):p−1​(C)→Cp|_{p^{-1}(C)}:p^{-1}(C)\to C where C=𝔸1∖{P1,…,Pr}C={\mathbb{A}}^{1}\setminus\{P_{1},\ldots,P_{r}\} is an affine line 𝔸1{\mathbb{A}}^{1} with rr points deleted off and that p−1​(Pi)p^{-1}(P_{i}) is a smooth (irreducible) variety for 1≤i≤r1\leq i\leq r. Then p−1​(Pi)p^{-1}(P_{i}) is acyclic for 1≤i≤r1\leq i\leq r.

Proof. Let X′=⋃i=1rp−1​(Pi)X^{\prime}=\bigcup_{i=1}^{r}p^{-1}(P_{i}). We have a long exact sequence of integral cohomology groups with compact support for a pair (X,X′)(X,X^{\prime})

⋯→Hc2​i​(X)→\displaystyle\cdots\to H^{2i}_{c}(X)\to Hc2​i​(X′)→Hc2​i+1​(X,X′)→\displaystyle H^{2i}_{c}(X^{\prime})\to H^{2i+1}_{c}(X,X^{\prime})\to
Hc2​i+1​(X)→Hc2​i+1​(X′)→Hc2​i+2​(X,X′)→⋯.\displaystyle H^{2i+1}_{c}(X)\to H^{2i+1}_{c}(X^{\prime})\to H^{2i+2}_{c}(X,X^{\prime})\to\cdots.

By the Poincaré duality, we have Hc2​i​(X)≅H2​n−2​i​(X)=0H^{2i}_{c}(X)\cong H_{2n-2i}(X)=0 and Hc2​i+1​(X)≅H2​n−2​i−1​(X)=0H^{2i+1}_{c}(X)\cong H_{2n-2i-1}(X)=0 for i≤n−1i\leq n-1. By the Lefschetz duality, Hc2​i+1​(X,X′)≅H2​n−2​i−1​(X∖X′)≅H2​n−2​i−1​(C)=0H^{2i+1}_{c}(X,X^{\prime})\cong H_{2n-2i-1}(X\setminus X^{\prime})\cong H_{2n-2i-1}(C)=0 and Hc2​i+2​(X,X′)≅H2​n−2​i−2​(X∖X′)≅H2​n−2​i−2​(C)=0H^{2i+2}_{c}(X,X^{\prime})\cong H_{2n-2i-2}(X\setminus X^{\prime})\cong H_{2n-2i-2}(C)=0 for i≤n−2i\leq n-2. Hence Hc2​i​(X′)≅H2​n−2−2​i​(X′)=0H^{2i}_{c}(X^{\prime})\cong H_{2n-2-2i}(X^{\prime})=0 and Hc2​i+1​(X′)≅H2​n−2​i−3​(X′)=0H^{2i+1}_{c}(X^{\prime})\cong H_{2n-2i-3}(X^{\prime})=0 for i≤n−2i\leq n-2. Thus Hj​(X′)=0H_{j}(X^{\prime})=0 for j≥1j\geq 1, and the assertion follows. ∎

Remark. Let XX be a smooth affine nn-fold for n≥3n\geq 3 and let p:X→𝔸1p:X\to{\mathbb{A}}^{1} and P1,…,PrP_{1},\ldots,P_{r} be as in Proposition 2.6. Then by the same argument as in the proof of [12, Theorem 2.3], XX is acyclic if p∗​(Pi)p^{*}(P_{i}) is reduced and p−1​(Pi)p^{-1}(P_{i}) is acyclic for every ii. Further, since π1​(X)\pi_{1}(X) is trivial by Nori [26], XX is contractible by a theorem of J. H. C. Whitehead.

3. GaG_{a}-equivariant affine modifications

We investigate GaG_{a}-actions on a factorial affine variety by GaG_{a}-equivariant affine modifications. We begin by recalling the definition of affine modification. For a general reference, we refer to [17].

Let BB be an affine ℂ{\mathbb{C}}-domain. Let RR be a subdomain of BB, II an ideal of RR, and ff a nonzero element of II. The subalgebra of the quotient field Q⁡(R)Q(R) generated by the elements a/fa/f for a∈Ia\in I is called the affine modification of RR along ff with center II and denoted by R⁡[f−1​I]R[f^{-1}I]. Suppose that BB is equipped with an lnd δ\delta restricting to RR such that δ⁡(f)=0\delta(f)=0. Then the ideal J=R∩f​BJ=R\cap fB of RR is δ\delta-stable, i.e., δ⁡(J)⊂J\delta(J)\subset J, and δ\delta restricts to R⁡[f−1​J]⊂BR[f^{-1}J]\subset B. The inclusions R↪R⁡[f−1​J]↪BR\hookrightarrow R[f^{-1}J]\hookrightarrow B yield a sequence of GaG_{a}-equivariant birational morphisms Spec​B→Spec​R​[f−1​J]→𝜎Spec​R{\rm Spec}\;B\to{\rm Spec}\;R[f^{-1}J]\xrightarrow{\sigma}{\rm Spec}\;R. The reduced divisor (f∘σ)∗​(0)(f\circ\sigma)^{*}(0) is called the exceptional divisor of σ\sigma.

In the following, BB is a factorial affine ℂ{\mathbb{C}}-domain equipped with an irreducible lnd δ\delta such that A=Ker​δA={\rm Ker}\>\delta is an affine ℂ{\mathbb{C}}-domain. Suppose that

pl⁡(δ)=fp​β​A{\rm pl}(\delta)=f^{p}\beta A (1)

where ff is a prime element of AA, p>0p>0, and β∈A\beta\in A and ff are coprime. Let z∈Bz\in B be a local slice such that δ⁡(z)=fp​β\delta(z)=f^{p}\beta. Then zz is not divisible by ff nor any prime factor of β\beta. Since B⁡[f−1​β−1]=A⁡[f−1​β−1]​[z]B[f^{-1}\beta^{-1}]=A[f^{-1}\beta^{-1}][z] and BB is finitely generated over ℂ{\mathbb{C}}, there exist positive integers μ\mu and γ\gamma such that

B=A⁡[z]​[f−μ​β−γ​J~]B=A[z][f^{-\mu}\beta^{-\gamma}\tilde{J}] (2)

where J~=A⁡[z]∩fμ​βγ​B\tilde{J}=A[z]\cap f^{\mu}\beta^{\gamma}B. Let

I=A⁡[z]∩fμ​BandB(1)=A⁡[z]​[f−μ​I].I=A[z]\cap f^{\mu}B\quad\text{and}\quad B^{(1)}=A[z][f^{-\mu}I].

Then

B=B(1)​[β−γ​J]whereJ=B(1)∩βγ​B.B=B^{(1)}[\beta^{-\gamma}J]\quad\text{where}\quad J=B^{(1)}\cap\beta^{\gamma}B.

Since II, JJ and J~\tilde{J} are δ\delta-stable ideals, we obtain a sequence of GaG_{a}-equivariant affine modifications

B0:=A⁡[z]⊂B(1)⊂B.B_{0}:=A[z]\subset B^{(1)}\subset B. (3)

Note that B0Ga=(B(1))Ga=BGa=AB_{0}^{G_{a}}=(B^{(1)})^{G_{a}}=B^{G_{a}}=A. Let X=Spec​BX={\rm Spec}\;B, X(1)=Spec​B(1)X^{(1)}={\rm Spec}\;B^{(1)} and X0=Spec​B0=Y×𝔸1X_{0}={\rm Spec}\;B_{0}=Y\times{\mathbb{A}}^{1} where Y=Spec​AY={\rm Spec}\;A. The sequence (3) yields a sequence of GaG_{a}-equivariant birational morphisms over YY

Theorem 3.5.

We have π|V⁡(xi)=τi∘πi\pi|_{V(x_{i})}=\tau_{i}\circ\pi_{i} where πi:V⁡(xi)→Spec​Ker​δi\pi_{i}:V(x_{i})\to{\rm Spec}\;{\rm Ker}\>\delta_{i} is the quotient morphism and τi:Spec​Ker​δi→Spec​A/xi​A\tau_{i}:{\rm Spec}\;{\rm Ker}\>\delta_{i}\to{\rm Spec}\;A/x_{i}A is the morphism defined by A/xi​A↪Ker​δiA/x_{i}A\hookrightarrow{\rm Ker}\>\delta_{i}. Remarks. (1) It holds that ei=pie_{i}=p_{i} for every ii. In fact, if 0<ei<pi0<e_{i}<p_{i} for some ii. Then δ(z−x1p1−e1⋯xipi−ei⋯xsps−esb)=0\delta(z-x_{1}^{p_{1}-e_{1}}\cdots x_{i}^{p_{i}-e_{i}}\cdots x_{s}^{p_{s}-e_{s}}b)=0 implies z−a∈xi​Bz-a\in x_{i}B for some a∈Aa\in A. This is a contradiction to the assumption. Hence ei=pie_{i}=p_{i} for every ii and pl⁡(δ)=α​A{\rm pl}(\delta)=\alpha A.

(2) Let AA be a factorial affine domain and B=A⁡[Y,Z]/(α​Y−g⁡(Z))B=A[Y,Z]/(\alpha Y-g(Z)) where A⁡[Y,Z]=A[2]A[Y,Z]=A^{[2]}, α∈A\alpha\in A and g⁡(Z)∈A⁡[Z]∖Ag(Z)\in A[Z]\setminus A is an irreducible polynomial. Then the factoriality of BB is studied in [4].

If B≅A[1]B\cong A^{[1]}, α​Y−g⁡(Z)\alpha Y-g(Z) is a coordinate of BB over (any ℚ{\mathbb{Q}}-algebra) AA by [28]. If A=k⁡[X1,…,Xm,T]=k[m+1]A=k[X_{1},\ldots,X_{m},T]=k^{[m+1]} for a field kk of characteristic 00 and g⁡(Z)=f⁡(Z,T)+h⁡(X1,…,Xm,T,Z)g(Z)=f(Z,T)+h(X_{1},\ldots,X_{m},T,Z) with f⁡(Z,T)∈k⁡[Z,T]f(Z,T)\in k[Z,T] and h⁡(X1,…,Xm,T,Z)∈k⁡[X1,…,Xm,T]h(X_{1},\ldots,X_{m},T,Z)\in k[X_{1},\ldots,X_{m},T] which is divided by every prime factor of α\alpha, criteria for B=k[m+2]B=k^{[m+2]} are given under some assumptions by [8].

4. Smooth acyclic affine varieties with free GaG_{a}-actions

First, we consider the case that XX is a smooth acyclic affine threefold with an 𝔸2{\mathbb{A}}^{2}-fibration f:X→𝔸1f:X\to{\mathbb{A}}^{1} and give a short proof to a characterization of 𝔸3{\mathbb{A}}^{3} due to Miyanishi [23], Kaliman [18].

Theorem 4.1.

Let X=Spec​BX={\rm Spec}\;B be a smooth acyclic affine threefold. If there exists an 𝔸2{\mathbb{A}}^{2}-fibration f:X→𝔸1f:X\to{\mathbb{A}}^{1} such that every closed fiber of ff is factorial, then X≅𝔸3X\cong{\mathbb{A}}^{3} and ff is a variable of B=ℂ[3]B={\mathbb{C}}^{[3]}.

Proof. By Fujita [7], XX is factorial and B∗=ℂ∗B^{*}={\mathbb{C}}^{*}. The existence of an 𝔸2{\mathbb{A}}^{2}-fibration f:X→𝔸1f:X\to{\mathbb{A}}^{1} implies that there exists β∈ℂ⁡[f]⊂B\beta\in{\mathbb{C}}[f]\subset B such that B⁡[β−1]=ℂ⁡[f,β−1,x,y]B[\beta^{-1}]={\mathbb{C}}[f,\beta^{-1},x,y], a polynomial ring in two variables over ℂ⁡[f,β−1]{\mathbb{C}}[f,\beta^{-1}]. Let DD be a ℂ⁡[f,β−1]{\mathbb{C}}[f,\beta^{-1}]-derivation on B⁡[β−1]B[\beta^{-1}] defined by D⁡(x)=1D(x)=1 and D⁡(y)=0D(y)=0. Then the derivation δ=βm​D\delta=\beta^{m}D restricts to an lnd on BB for some integer m≥0m\geq 0 since BB is finitely generated over ℂ{\mathbb{C}}. We may assume δ\delta is irreducible. Let A=Ker​δA={\rm Ker}\>\delta. Then AA is factorial and A∗=B∗=ℂ∗A^{*}=B^{*}={\mathbb{C}}^{*}. Further, f∈Af\in A and δ⁡(x)\delta(x) is a product of some factors of β\beta. Hence the 𝔸2{\mathbb{A}}^{2}-fibration f:X→𝔸1f:X\to{\mathbb{A}}^{1} is equivariant with respect to the GaG_{a}-action associated with δ\delta and A⁡[β−1]=ℂ⁡[f,β−1,y]A[\beta^{-1}]={\mathbb{C}}[f,\beta^{-1},y]. The GaG_{a}-equivariant 𝔸2{\mathbb{A}}^{2}-fibration f:X→𝔸1f:X\to{\mathbb{A}}^{1} splits as a composite of the quotient morphism π:X→Y\pi:X\to Y and fY:Y→𝔸1f_{Y}:Y\to{\mathbb{A}}^{1}. Since fY:Y→𝔸1f_{Y}:Y\to{\mathbb{A}}^{1} is an 𝔸1{\mathbb{A}}^{1}-fibration, A=ℂ[2]A={\mathbb{C}}^{[2]} by a characterization of affine plane [22] and ff is a variable of AA. For every c∈ℂc\in{\mathbb{C}}, the fiber Wc=Spec​B/(f−c)​BW_{c}={\rm Spec}\;B/(f-c)B of ff is factorial and has a non-trivial GaG_{a}-action induced by δ\delta. The lnd δc\delta_{c} on B/(f−c)​BB/(f-c)B induced by δ\delta is written as δc=ac​dc\delta_{c}=a_{c}d_{c} for an irreducible lnd dcd_{c} on B/(f−c)​BB/(f-c)B and ac∈Ker​dca_{c}\in{\rm Ker}\>d_{c}. Consider the GaG_{a}-action on WcW_{c} associated with dcd_{c}. By Lemma 2.1, WcW_{c} is smooth. Further, by Proposition 2.6, each WcW_{c} is acyclic, hence Wc≅𝔸2W_{c}\cong{\mathbb{A}}^{2} by Miyanishi [24]. By [13, Theorem 2.1.16], [27], f:X→𝔸1f:X\to{\mathbb{A}}^{1} is an 𝔸2{\mathbb{A}}^{2}-bundle, and hence X≅𝔸3X\cong{\mathbb{A}}^{3} and ff is a variable. ∎

Remark. The existence of an 𝔸2{\mathbb{A}}^{2}-fibration f:X→𝔸1f:X\to{\mathbb{A}}^{1} is equivalent to the existence of an 𝔸2{\mathbb{A}}^{2}-cylinder U≅C×𝔸2U\cong C\times{\mathbb{A}}^{2} in XX for an affine curve CC ([23], [18]). The above proof of Theorem 4.1 shows that if a smooth acyclic affine threefold XX contains an 𝔸2{\mathbb{A}}^{2}-cylinder UU and each irreducible component of X∖UX\setminus U is factorial, then X≅𝔸3X\cong{\mathbb{A}}^{3}.

Let XX be as in Theorem 4.1 and suppose that XX has a GaG_{a}-action and a GaG_{a}-equivariant 𝔸2{\mathbb{A}}^{2}-fibration f:X→𝔸1f:X\to{\mathbb{A}}^{1} where GaG_{a} acts trivially on 𝔸1{\mathbb{A}}^{1}. Theorem 4.1 does not imply that the quotient morphism π:X→Y=𝔸2\pi:X\to Y={\mathbb{A}}^{2} is an 𝔸1{\mathbb{A}}^{1}-bundle as the following simple example shows.

Example 4.1   Let B=ℂ⁡[x,y,z]B={\mathbb{C}}[x,y,z] be a polynomial ring and let X=Spec​BX={\rm Spec}\;B. Define an lnd δ\delta on BB by δ⁡(x)=0\delta(x)=0, δ⁡(y)=−2​z\delta(y)=-2z, δ⁡(z)=x2\delta(z)=x^{2}. Then A=Ker​δ=ℂ⁡[x,t]=ℂ[2]A={\rm Ker}\>\delta={\mathbb{C}}[x,t]={\mathbb{C}}^{[2]} where t=x2​y+z2t=x^{2}y+z^{2} and let Y=Spec​AY={\rm Spec}\;A. The quotient morphism π:X→Y\pi:X\to Y is faithfully flat with Sing⁡(π)≠∅{\rm Sing}(\pi)\neq\emptyset. In fact, Sing⁡(π){\rm Sing}(\pi) is the closed set V⁡(x)≅𝔸1V(x)\cong{\mathbb{A}}^{1} of Y=𝔸(x,t)2Y={\mathbb{A}}^{2}_{(x,t)}. For Q=(0,β)∈V⁡(x)Q=(0,\beta)\in V(x), the fiber π∗​(Q)\pi^{*}(Q) is 𝔸1∐𝔸1{\mathbb{A}}^{1}\amalg{\mathbb{A}}^{1} if β≠0\beta\neq 0 and 𝔸1{\mathbb{A}}^{1} with multiplicity 22 if β=0\beta=0. The fixed point locus consists of the fiber π−1​(O)\pi^{-1}(O) for O=(0,0)∈YO=(0,0)\in Y. The projection x:X→𝔸1x:X\to{\mathbb{A}}^{1} is an trivial 𝔸2{\mathbb{A}}^{2}-bundle and xx is a variable of BB, however, π:X→Y\pi:X\to Y is not an 𝔸1{\mathbb{A}}^{1}-bundle.

Let X=Spec​BX={\rm Spec}\;B be an affine variety of dimension ≥3\geq 3 with a GaG_{a}-action and a GaG_{a}-equivariant fibration f:X→𝔸1f:X\to{\mathbb{A}}^{1} where GaG_{a} acts trivially on 𝔸1{\mathbb{A}}^{1}. Let π:X→Y=Spec​A\pi:X\to Y={\rm Spec}\;A be the quotient morphism with A=Ker​δA={\rm Ker}\>\delta where δ\delta is the lnd on BB associated with the GaG_{a}-action. Since f:X→𝔸1f:X\to{\mathbb{A}}^{1} is GaG_{a}-equivariant, f∈Af\in A defines the morphism fY:Y→𝔸1f_{Y}:Y\to{\mathbb{A}}^{1} and ff splits as X→πY→fY𝔸1X\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\pi}}{{\to}}Y\stackrel{{\scriptstyle f_{Y}}}{{\to}}{\mathbb{A}}^{1}. For c∈ℂc\in{\mathbb{C}}, let Yc=fY−1​(c)Y_{c}=f_{Y}^{-1}(c) and Wc=f−1​(c)W_{c}=f^{-1}(c). The GaG_{a}-action restricts to Wc=Spec​B/(f−c)​BW_{c}={\rm Spec}\;B/(f-c)B. Let πc:Wc→Zc=Spec​Ker​δc\pi_{c}:W_{c}\to Z_{c}={\rm Spec}\;{\rm Ker}\>\delta_{c} be the quotient morphism where δc\delta_{c} is the induced lnd on B/(f−c)​BB/(f-c)B. Then the restriction π|Wc:Wc→Yc\pi|_{W_{c}}:W_{c}\to Y_{c} splits as π|Wc=νc∘πc\pi|_{W_{c}}=\nu_{c}\circ\pi_{c} where νc:Zc→Yc=Spec​A/(f−c)​A\nu_{c}:Z_{c}\to Y_{c}={\rm Spec}\;A/(f-c)A is the morphism defined by the inclusion A/(f−c)​A↪Ker​δcA/(f-c)A\hookrightarrow{\rm Ker}\>\delta_{c}. As for the singular locus Sing⁡(π){\rm Sing}(\pi), we have the following result.

Lemma 4.2.

Let X=Spec​BX={\rm Spec}\;B be a smooth factorial affine variety of dimension n≥3n\geq 3 with a free GaG_{a}-action. Let π:X→Y\pi:X\to Y be the quotient morphism. We assume that Y=Spec​AY={\rm Spec}\;A is an affine variety and π\pi is surjective and equi-dimensional. Suppose that there exists a GaG_{a}-equivariant fibration f:X→𝔸1f:X\to{\mathbb{A}}^{1} with a trivial GaG_{a}-action on 𝔸1{\mathbb{A}}^{1} such that a general closed fiber FF of ff is GaG_{a}-equivariantly isomorphic to Z×𝔸1Z\times{\mathbb{A}}^{1} where GaG_{a} acts on an affine variety ZZ trivially and on the second factor 𝔸1{\mathbb{A}}^{1} by translation. Then Sing⁡(π)=∅{\rm Sing}(\pi)=\emptyset or Sing⁡(π)¯\overline{{\rm Sing}(\pi)} is a union of finite fibers of fY:Y→𝔸1f_{Y}:Y\to{\mathbb{A}}^{1}.

Proof. Let δ\delta be the lnd on BB associated with the GaG_{a}-action. Then δ\delta is irreducible since the action is free, and A=Ker​δA={\rm Ker}\>\delta is an affine ℂ{\mathbb{C}}-domain by the assumption. By Proposition 2.5, Y=Spec​AY={\rm Spec}\;A is a smooth factorial affine variety and Sing⁡(π){\rm Sing}(\pi) is of pure codimension one unless Sing⁡(π)=∅{\rm Sing}(\pi)=\emptyset. Suppose that Sing⁡(π)≠∅{\rm Sing}(\pi)\neq\emptyset. As remarked above, f∈Af\in A defines the morphism fY:Y→𝔸1f_{Y}:Y\to{\mathbb{A}}^{1} and f=fY∘πf=f_{Y}\circ\pi. Choose λ∈ℂ\lambda\in{\mathbb{C}} so that Yλ=Spec​A/(f−λ)​AY_{\lambda}={\rm Spec}\;A/(f-\lambda)A and Wλ=Spec​B/(f−λ)​BW_{\lambda}={\rm Spec}\;B/(f-\lambda)B are general fibers of fY:Y→𝔸1f_{Y}:Y\to{\mathbb{A}}^{1} and f:X→𝔸1f:X\to{\mathbb{A}}^{1}, respectively. Then Wλ=π−1​(Yλ)W_{\lambda}=\pi^{-1}(Y_{\lambda}) and YλY_{\lambda} are smooth by Bertini’s theorem. Let δλ\delta_{\lambda} be the lnd on B/(f−λ)​BB/(f-\lambda)B induced by δ\delta and let Zλ=Spec​Ker​δλZ_{\lambda}={\rm Spec}\;{\rm Ker}\>\delta_{\lambda}. By the assumption, δλ\delta_{\lambda} has a slice, hence ZλZ_{\lambda} is an affine variety. The restriction π|Wλ:Wλ→Yλ\pi|_{W_{\lambda}}:W_{\lambda}\to Y_{\lambda} is a composite of the quotient morphism πλ:Wλ→Zλ\pi_{\lambda}:W_{\lambda}\to Z_{\lambda} and a surjective morphism νλ:Zλ→Yλ\nu_{\lambda}:Z_{\lambda}\to Y_{\lambda} which is defined by the inclusion A/(f−λ)​A↪Ker​δλA/(f-\lambda)A\hookrightarrow{\rm Ker}\>\delta_{\lambda}. Note that Q⁡(Ker​δλ)Q({\rm Ker}\>\delta_{\lambda}) is an algebraic extension of Q⁡(A/(f−λ)​A)Q(A/(f-\lambda)A). Since the GaG_{a}-action is free, every closed fiber of π\pi is a disjoint union of finite GaG_{a}-orbits. Further, since WλW_{\lambda} is GaG_{a}-equivariantly isomorphic to Zλ×𝔸1Z_{\lambda}\times{\mathbb{A}}^{1} and πλ:Wλ→Zλ\pi_{\lambda}:W_{\lambda}\to Z_{\lambda} is a trivial 𝔸1{\mathbb{A}}^{1}-bundle, every fiber of νλ\nu_{\lambda} consists of finite points. Since YλY_{\lambda} is a general fiber of fY:Y→𝔸1f_{Y}:Y\to{\mathbb{A}}^{1}, Yλ⊄Sing⁡(π)¯Y_{\lambda}\not\subset\overline{{\rm Sing}(\pi)}, which implies that a general fiber of π|Wλ\pi|_{W_{\lambda}} is 𝔸1{\mathbb{A}}^{1} (cf. [20]). Hence νλ\nu_{\lambda} is birational, and ZλZ_{\lambda} coincides with YλY_{\lambda} by Zariski’s Main Theorem. Then π|Wλ\pi|_{W_{\lambda}} coincides with the quotient morphism πλ:Wλ→Zλ\pi_{\lambda}:W_{\lambda}\to Z_{\lambda} which is a trivial 𝔸1{\mathbb{A}}^{1}-bundle by the assumption. Thus Yλ∩Sing⁡(π)=∅Y_{\lambda}\cap{\rm Sing}(\pi)=\emptyset for general λ\lambda and Sing⁡(π)¯\overline{{\rm Sing}(\pi)} is a union of finite fibers Yci=Spec​A/(f−ci)​AY_{c_{i}}={\rm Spec}\;A/(f-c_{i})A for ci∈ℂc_{i}\in{\mathbb{C}} and 1≤i≤s1\leq i\leq s. ∎

By Theorem 4.1 and Lemma 4.2, we obtain the following result.

Theorem 4.3.

Let X=Spec​BX={\rm Spec}\;B be a smooth acyclic affine fourfold with a free GaG_{a}-action. Let π:X→Y\pi:X\to Y be the quotient morphism where we assume Y=Spec​AY={\rm Spec}\;A is an affine variety. If

  1. (1)

    π\pi is equi-dimensional and surjective,

  2. (2)

    YY is acyclic,

  3. (3)

    there exists a GaG_{a}-equivariant 𝔸3{\mathbb{A}}^{3}-fibration f:X→𝔸1f:X\to{\mathbb{A}}^{1} where the GaG_{a}-action on 𝔸1{\mathbb{A}}^{1} is trivial such that every closed fiber of the induced morphism fY:Y→𝔸1f_{Y}:Y\to{\mathbb{A}}^{1} is factorial,

then Y≅𝔸3Y\cong{\mathbb{A}}^{3} and ff is a variable of A=ℂ[3]A={\mathbb{C}}^{[3]}.

Further, suppose that

  1. (4)

    the morphism νc:Zc=Spec​Ker​δc→Yc=Spec​A/(f−c)​A\nu_{c}:Z_{c}={\rm Spec}\;{\rm Ker}\>\delta_{c}\to Y_{c}={\rm Spec}\;A/(f-c)A defined by the inclusion A/(f−c)​A↪Ker​δcA/(f-c)A\hookrightarrow{\rm Ker}\>\delta_{c} is birational for every c∈ℂc\in{\mathbb{C}}. Here, δc\delta_{c} is the induced lnd on B/(f−c)​BB/(f-c)B.

Then π:X→Y\pi:X\to Y is a trivial 𝔸1{\mathbb{A}}^{1}-bundle and X≅𝔸4X\cong{\mathbb{A}}^{4}.

Proof. Since X=Spec​BX={\rm Spec}\;B is smooth and acyclic, BB is factorial and B∗=ℂ∗B^{*}={\mathbb{C}}^{*}. Let δ\delta be an irreducible lnd on BB associated with the GaG_{a}-action and let A=Ker​δA={\rm Ker}\>\delta which is an affine ℂ{\mathbb{C}}-domain by the assumption. By Proposition 2.5, Y=Spec​AY={\rm Spec}\;A is a smooth factorial affine threefold. The quotient morphism π:X→Y\pi:X\to Y is faithfully flat by the condition (1). The morphism fY:Y→𝔸1f_{Y}:Y\to{\mathbb{A}}^{1} induced by ff is a surjection. In fact, if f−1​(c)=∅f^{-1}(c)=\emptyset for some c∈ℂc\in{\mathbb{C}}, then the ideal (f−c)​A(f-c)A is a unit ideal, which implies f−c∈A∗=B∗=ℂ∗f-c\in A^{*}=B^{*}={\mathbb{C}}^{*}. This is a contradiction. Hence fY:Y→𝔸1f_{Y}:Y\to{\mathbb{A}}^{1} is surjective and so is ff. For c∈ℂc\in{\mathbb{C}}, let Yc=Spec​A/(f−c)​AY_{c}={\rm Spec}\;A/(f-c)A and Wc=π−1​(Yc)=Spec​B/(f−c)​BW_{c}=\pi^{-1}(Y_{c})={\rm Spec}\;B/(f-c)B. As observed above, π|Wc=νc∘πc\pi|_{W_{c}}=\nu_{c}\circ\pi_{c} where πc:Wc→Zc\pi_{c}:W_{c}\to Z_{c} is the quotient morphism. For a general c∈ℂc\in{\mathbb{C}}, Wc≅𝔸3W_{c}\cong{\mathbb{A}}^{3} and GaG_{a} acts freely on it. Hence for a general c∈ℂc\in{\mathbb{C}}, Zc≅𝔸2Z_{c}\cong{\mathbb{A}}^{2} and Wc≅Zc×𝔸1W_{c}\cong Z_{c}\times{\mathbb{A}}^{1} by Kaliman [15]. By the same argument as in the proof of Lemma 4.2, Yc=Zc≅𝔸2Y_{c}=Z_{c}\cong{\mathbb{A}}^{2} for a general c∈ℂc\in{\mathbb{C}} and fY:Y→𝔸1f_{Y}:Y\to{\mathbb{A}}^{1} is an 𝔸2{\mathbb{A}}^{2}-fibration. Since YcY_{c} is factorial for every c∈ℂc\in{\mathbb{C}} and YY is acyclic by the conditions (2) and (3), Y≅𝔸3Y\cong{\mathbb{A}}^{3} and ff is a variable of A=ℂ[3]A={\mathbb{C}}^{[3]} by Theorem 4.1.

By Lemma 4.2, we have Sing⁡(π)≠∅{\rm Sing}(\pi)\neq\emptyset or Sing⁡(π)¯\overline{{\rm Sing}(\pi)} consists of finite fibers of fYf_{Y}. If the condition (4) is satisfied, then π\pi is a trivial 𝔸1{\mathbb{A}}^{1}-bundle by Theorem 3.6 and the assertion follows. ∎

If GaG_{a} acts non-trivially on X=𝔸4X={\mathbb{A}}^{4} and preserves a coordinate xx, i.e., δ⁡(x)=0\delta(x)=0 for the lnd δ\delta associated with the GaG_{a}-action on XX, A=Ker​δA={\rm Ker}\>\delta is an affine ℂ{\mathbb{C}}-domain by Bhatwadekar and Daigle [1] and Y=Spec​AY={\rm Spec}\;A is an affine threefold. By considering the projection x:X→𝔸1x:X\to{\mathbb{A}}^{1} as the 𝔸3{\mathbb{A}}^{3}-fibration ff in Theorem 4.3, we obtain the following result of a free GaG_{a}-action on 𝔸4{\mathbb{A}}^{4} preserving a coordinate.

Corollary 4.4.

Let GaG_{a} act freely on X=𝔸4X={\mathbb{A}}^{4} preserving a coordinate xx of XX. Suppose that the quotient morphism π:X→Y\pi:X\to Y is equi-dimensional and surjective and YY is acyclic. If every closed fiber of the induced morphism x:Y→𝔸1x:Y\to{\mathbb{A}}^{1} is factorial, then Y≅𝔸3Y\cong{\mathbb{A}}^{3} and xx is a coordinate of YY.

Example 4.2   Let X0X_{0} be a Koras-Russell 33-fold defined by X2​Y−g⁡(X,Z,T)=0X^{2}Y-g(X,Z,T)=0 in 𝔸(X,Y,Z,T)4{\mathbb{A}}^{4}_{(X,Y,Z,T)} where g⁡(X,Z,T)=X+Z2+T3g(X,Z,T)=X+Z^{2}+T^{3} and let X~=X0×𝔸1\tilde{X}=X_{0}\times{\mathbb{A}}^{1}. Then X~\tilde{X} is a smooth acyclic affine fourfold. Let B=ℂ⁡[X,Y,Z,T,W]/(X2​Y−g⁡(X,T,Z))B={\mathbb{C}}[X,Y,Z,T,W]/(X^{2}Y-g(X,T,Z)) where ℂ⁡[X,Y,Z,T,W]{\mathbb{C}}[X,Y,Z,T,W] is a polynomial ring in 55 variables and we regard BB as the coordinate ring of X~\tilde{X}. We denote the residue class of X,Y,Z,T,WX,Y,Z,T,W by x,y,z,t,w∈Bx,y,z,t,w\in B, respectively. Define an lnd δ\delta on BB by

δ⁡(x)=δ⁡(t)=0,δ⁡(y)=2​z,δ⁡(z)=x2,δ⁡(w)=1.\delta(x)=\delta(t)=0,\quad\delta(y)=2z,\quad\delta(z)=x^{2},\quad\delta(w)=1.

Since δ\delta has a slice ww, the GaG_{a}-action associated with δ\delta on X~\tilde{X} is free and B=A⁡[w]B=A[w] where A=Ker​δA={\rm Ker}\>\delta. We have

A=ℂ⁡[x,u,v,t]≅ℂ⁡[X,U,V,T]/(X2​U−g⁡(X,V,T))A={\mathbb{C}}[x,u,v,t]\cong{\mathbb{C}}[X,U,V,T]/(X^{2}U-g(X,V,T))

where u=y−2​z​w+x2​w2u=y-2zw+x^{2}w^{2} and v=z−x2​wv=z-x^{2}w. Hence Y=Spec​A≅X0Y={\rm Spec}\;A\cong X_{0} is a smooth acyclic threefold. The function x∈Bx\in B defines a GaG_{a}-equivariant 𝔸3{\mathbb{A}}^{3}-fibration x:X~→𝔸1x:\tilde{X}\to{\mathbb{A}}^{1}. The induced morphism xY:Y→𝔸1x_{Y}:Y\to{\mathbb{A}}^{1} is an 𝔸2{\mathbb{A}}^{2}-fibration with a single singular fiber xY−1​(0)≅C×𝔸1x_{Y}^{-1}(0)\cong C\times{\mathbb{A}}^{1} for the cuspidal curve V2+T3=0V^{2}+T^{3}=0 in 𝔸(V,T)2{\mathbb{A}}^{2}_{(V,T)}, which is non-normal. The quotient morphism π:X~→Y\pi:\tilde{X}\to Y is a trivial 𝔸1{\mathbb{A}}^{1}-bundle, but Y≇𝔸3Y\not\cong{\mathbb{A}}^{3}.

At the present, whether X~\tilde{X} is isomorphic to 𝔸4{\mathbb{A}}^{4} or not is unknown. If X~=X×𝔸1≅𝔸4\tilde{X}=X\times{\mathbb{A}}^{1}\cong{\mathbb{A}}^{4}, we obtain a negative answer to the Cancellation Problem which asks whether X×𝔸1≅𝔸n+1X\times{\mathbb{A}}^{1}\cong{\mathbb{A}}^{n+1} implies X≅𝔸nX\cong{\mathbb{A}}^{n} or not.

Theorem 4.3 leads to the following question.

Question  Let XX be a smooth acyclic affine fourfold with a free GaG_{a}-action. Under the assumptions (1)–(3) in Theorem 4.3, X≅𝔸4X\cong{\mathbb{A}}^{4}?
